neighbours.label: present-perfect reports of a continuing or newly reached state ('has now', 'has proven itself')
fire: The young striker has now scored in seven consecutive matches for the club.
This old proof technique has proven itself remarkably useful in modern number theory.
Since the merger, the company has now closed nine of its regional offices.
The drought has now lasted longer than any other in the state's recorded history.
Our little garden has proven itself able to survive the harsh mountain winters.
With this win, the team has now reached the final three years in a row.
The vaccine has proven itself safe across several large trials in older adults.
The museum has now welcomed more than a million visitors since its reopening.
quiet: The young striker scored in seven consecutive matches for the club last year.
This old proof technique was taught in the first week of the course.
Before the merger, the company opened nine regional offices in the south.
The drought lasted three years in the 1950s, according to the records.
Our little garden produced tomatoes and beans in the warm summer of 2015.
With that win, the team reached the final for the first time in 1987.
The vaccine was tested in several large trials in older adults.
The museum welcomed its first visitors on a rainy afternoon in May.

predictions: Weak in probing: present-perfect updates may reach ~0.2-0.35, simple-past versions lower. Likely fails on median.
notes: Probe: 'has proven itself to be very hard' 0.362, 'have now lost eleven straight' 0.202, 'continues to roam' 0.099, 'have attended' 0.038; simple past 'lost eleven straight games last season' 0.060. Card peaks on ' now', ' have', ' been'. Contrast is weak.
